title: 2004 AMC 8 Problem 25
statement: Two \(4 \times 4\) squares intersect at right angles, bisecting their intersecting sides, as shown. The circle’s diameter is the segment between the two points of intersection. What is the area of the shaded region created by removing the circle from the squares?

solutions.text:
The two \(4\times4\) squares have total area \(32,\) but their overlap is a \(2\times2\) square with area \(4.\) Thus the area covered by the union of the two squares is \(32-4=28.\)

The circle’s diameter is the diagonal of that \(2\times2\) overlap square, so the diameter is \(2\sqrt2\) and the radius is \(\sqrt2.\)

The circle area is \(\pi(\sqrt2)^2=2\pi,\) so the shaded area is \(28-2\pi.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Find the area covered by the union of the two squares.
The circle diameter is the diagonal of the \(2\times2\) overlap square.
